correctness.rationale: Every distinct factor either is constant, contains one 01 transition or contains the unique central 10 transition. The unique 10 adjacent pair forces any attractor to select its U or V position, and then all multi-transition factors are covered. Longest constant runs suffice for constant factors. One-transition 01 factors correspond to union of two integer rectangles [1,a]×[1,b], [1,c]×[1,d]. Four explicit two-position witnesses cover the aligned-maxima cases and crossed cases with one run-length excess≤1. The remaining (a>c,d>b) regime has three disjoint forced factors; for (c≥a+2,b≥d+2), a chosen central U or V leaves an explicit 01 factor inaccessible to any second position. Two explicit three-position sets cover all other words. Disjoint parameterizations of those two obstruction regions give the rational generating function and dominant pole ratio 1/2. Independent direct factor-occurrence-mask enumeration tested all 625 quadruples with lengths 1..5, plus exact coefficient comparisons for n=4..18. These are finite checks; the proof exhausts all positive run lengths.
risks: A four-run restriction is essential: no theorem for arbitrary runs or full set of optimal position combinations.
Finite factor-mask enumeration is not an unbounded combinatorial proof.

value.rationale: Exactly four alternating runs are the first natural run-complexity setting with a nontrivial two-versus-three alphabet-lower-bound transition. A complete four-parameter decision with explicit optimal witnesses, exact enumeration and limiting density is a self-contained useful combinatorial classification, not an arbitrary sample.
risks: Exactly four nonempty alternating runs, with all positive lengths. No classification of all optimal hitting sets or any higher-run grammar.

final_claim: For all positive integers a,b,c,d, the minimum string-attractor size of w=0^a1^b0^c1^d is 3 exactly if (a>c and d>b) or (c>=a+2 and b>=d+2), otherwise 2. Counting both initial symbols, the generating function for 3-attractor four-run words is 2z^6(1+z²)/[(1−z)²(1−z²)²], and the asymptotic fraction is 1/2.
limitations: Exactly four nonempty alternating runs, with all positive lengths. No classification of all optimal hitting sets or any higher-run grammar.
